name: Objects and Light
summary: A visitor identity that offers a small number of ways to look without telling the viewer what to feel.

recognitionRules: Pair Optima interpretation with Futura navigational labels.
Use object numbers as stable anchors from image to caption.
Give each looking prompt its own space.
Keep interpretation distinct from object facts and provenance.
Use rust object labels and route links with dark interpretation text; isolate each object image and its caption.

principles: Invite attention before offering interpretation; keep object facts and imaginative response distinct.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: Three forms. Three ways to look. Take the time you need.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid prescribing a viewer’s feelings or implying unverified provenance.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: Look at the edge, then read the record.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use OBJECTS AND LIGHT in Optima with a small offset line beneath LIGHT. No sunburst; leave the visual field to the objects.
invariants: Pair Optima interpretation with Futura navigational labels.
Use object numbers as stable anchors from image to caption.
Give each looking prompt its own space.
adaptations: A pocket guide can use one object per panel.
An exhibition label keeps one looking prompt and the essential record.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.

clearSpaceRule: Keep one half of the main wordmark cap height clear around the full silhouette, including its source-derived supporting device.
